title: Pay yourself first
description: Move a little to savings when money arrives, before spending starts — here is the gentle version.

body.heading: The order matters
paragraphs: Many people save what is left after spending — and often nothing is left. 'Pay yourself first' flips the order: when money arrives, move a small amount to savings straight away, then live on the rest.
Start tiny. The habit of moving money first matters more than the amount, and you can raise it when income grows or costs fall.

body.heading: Be realistic, stay kind
paragraphs: If you move too much and have to pull it back for essentials every month, the system — not you — needs adjusting. Lower the amount until it sticks.
Some months, paying yourself first might mean $1 or even pausing. A flexible habit you keep beats a strict one you quit.

body.heading: Pair it with payday
paragraphs: Attach the transfer to the moment money lands: payday, allowance day, or the day a payment clears. Same trigger, same small action, every time.

takeaway: When money arrives, move a small amount to savings first — then spend the rest without guilt.
